provenance: Original development pitches created for this project. Scores are author judgments, not audience evidence. No scenario has been user-selected or production-tested.

scenarios.title: The Dry Seat
scenarios.logline: A commuter seems to reserve a bench with a coat, then removes it to offer a dry seat to a rain-soaked stranger.
scenarios.setup: Under a bus shelter, a seated commuter guards a coat spread across the adjacent bench.
scenarios.turn: A soaked adult approaches; the commuter lifts the coat, revealing the dry rectangle beneath.
scenarios.landing: An open palm offers the seat; the stranger sits and they exchange a small relieved smile.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Show coat lift in medium two-shot; cut after the invitation and use a settled final pose rather than a complex sitting motion.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A visible dry patch explains the choice; a familiar kindness mechanism lowers originality but simplifies execution.

scenarios.title: Small Shelter
scenarios.logline: A woman seems to protect a shopping bag from rain; lowering it reveals she has made a roof for a sleeping puppy.
scenarios.setup: An adult holds a broad empty paper shopping bag over a low wall while rain wets her sleeve.
scenarios.turn: A gentle downward reveal shows the puppy sheltered beneath the bag, not shopping inside it.
scenarios.landing: She adjusts the shelter toward the puppy and accepts the rain on her own shoulder.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use a rigid folded cardboard cover instead of a deforming bag if needed; puppy remains resting and safe.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Readable protection with a crowded human-animal kindness trope; no animal distress is needed.

scenarios.title: The Returned Cart
scenarios.logline: A hurried customer turns back to return a trolley, allowing an exhausted worker to sit for a moment.
scenarios.setup: A worker approaches a stray trolley while a departing customer notices the worker rubbing a tired shoulder.
scenarios.turn: The customer reverses direction and pushes the trolley into its bay.
scenarios.landing: The worker lowers onto a nearby stool; the customer gives a quiet nod.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Keep trolley movement short and straight; fatigue is a visible pause, not an unexplained medical event.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Grounded and inexpensive but its emotional stakes may be too slight without a strong performance.

scenarios.title: The Open Gate
scenarios.logline: A neighbour opens a narrow gate wider, letting a person carrying a large plant pass without damaging it.
scenarios.setup: An adult struggles to angle a leafy plant through a half-open garden gate.
scenarios.turn: A neighbour stops their own task and folds both gate panels fully back.
scenarios.landing: The plant passes intact; a single fallen leaf is gently returned.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Skip the leaf handoff if contact fails; end on a grateful look through the open gate.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A subtle connection rather than a twist; may fit a quiet series but not a high-contrast pilot.

scenarios.title: The Shared Shade
scenarios.logline: A vendor rotates an umbrella away from their own stall to shade the neighbour's sleeping face.
scenarios.setup: A vendor pauses in midday sun and looks toward the next stall.
scenarios.turn: The umbrella rotates, revealing an exhausted neighbour sleeping on folded arms.
scenarios.landing: The shadow settles across the sleeper; the first vendor quietly returns to work in partial sun.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Design two approved shadow states and edit between them rather than demanding a physically exact traveling shadow.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A specific visual sacrifice; shadow control is its principal production risk.

scenarios.title: A Place for Two
scenarios.logline: An older adult sets two cups at an empty table; a younger relative arrives and warms the waiting hands.
scenarios.setup: Two cups and an empty chair; the older adult's hands rest around the untouched second cup.
scenarios.turn: The younger relative enters the frame and occupies the waiting chair.
scenarios.landing: Their hands settle together around one cup; both look up.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use a simple side-by-side final composition and one clear entrance; do not imply bereavement without evidence.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Warm and legible, but two-cup imagery is familiar and the relationship is not self-proving.

scenarios.title: The Second Button
scenarios.logline: One partner struggles with a coat button; the other quietly offers their own misbuttoned coat for help.
scenarios.setup: One adult fumbles a coat fastening while the partner watches with affection.
scenarios.turn: The partner reveals their own coat is also crooked, asking for help with a small gesture.
scenarios.landing: They laugh silently and straighten each other's lapels.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Show crooked lapels rather than detailed threading; keep the comic reaction visible.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Reciprocal care avoids a one-way rescue but relies on small gestures reading on a phone.

scenarios.title: The Warm Side
scenarios.logline: Two siblings dispute a blanket, then turn it sideways and discover there is room for both.
scenarios.setup: Two adults at opposite ends of a short blanket pull it gently toward themselves.
scenarios.turn: One stops, rotates the blanket and opens the free side toward the other.
scenarios.landing: They settle shoulder to shoulder, sharing its full width.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Cut between two stable cloth states; do not require a continuous complex fabric rotation.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Clear mutual adjustment, with fabric continuity keeping feasibility below a simple prop reveal.

scenarios.title: The Spare Helmet
scenarios.logline: A rider appears to leave alone, then turns back with a spare helmet for a waiting friend.
scenarios.setup: A stationary scooter rider checks the empty rear seat while a friend stands back.
scenarios.turn: A second helmet emerges from the open storage compartment.
scenarios.landing: The friend accepts it with a grin; the scooter remains parked.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: No riding stunt; end before fitting or mounting and keep the vehicle still.
scenarios.scoreRationale: An economical inclusion story, but the opening must not falsely suggest abandonment.

scenarios.title: The Waiting Plate
scenarios.logline: A late worker finds a covered plate and a housemate asleep beside the table, still keeping them company.
scenarios.setup: A tired adult enters a dim kitchen and notices a covered plate.
scenarios.turn: A slight reframe reveals the housemate asleep at the other end of the table.
scenarios.landing: The returning worker lowers a blanket over the sleeper before sitting.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use a small cloth drape and two characters only; no explanatory clock or readable note.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Reciprocal care with a strong final action; a clear table layout is essential.

scenarios.title: The Worn Step
scenarios.logline: A person leaves space on a worn doorstep, then rests a hand on the empty place without explaining the absence.
scenarios.setup: A person sits on one half of a wide doorstep and shifts to make room.
scenarios.turn: The doorway stays empty; the camera settles on the unused place.
scenarios.landing: An open hand rests on the stone beside them, followed by a quiet breath.
risks: absence may read as nothing happening
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use as a subtle mood study, not a first high-comprehension pilot; cold-viewer testing is decisive.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Technically easy but meaning is underdetermined without backstory.

scenarios.title: The Unplayed Duet
scenarios.logline: A pianist leaves one half of a bench empty and plays only their half of a familiar duet.
scenarios.setup: A musician sits on one half of a two-person piano bench.
scenarios.turn: Their gaze moves to the unused keys and the vacant half of the bench.
scenarios.landing: The hand hovers, then rests where the other player's hand would have been.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Not suitable for this silent-first launch without a new visual premise.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Emotionally promising in longer form, but music supplies the missing relationship information.

scenarios.title: The Other Glove
scenarios.logline: A person finds a mismatched glove in an old coat and holds it against their cheek.
scenarios.setup: A person searches a worn coat pocket and pulls out one much smaller glove.
scenarios.turn: The glove fits neither their hand nor the coat's practical purpose.
scenarios.landing: They stop searching and hold the glove gently, smiling through the pause.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Keep glove silhouette large and clear; do not assume viewers infer death or parenthood.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A tactile memory can work, but the source of longing is deliberately uncertain.

scenarios.title: The Still-Warm Mug
scenarios.logline: A hand reaches toward an empty chair; steam briefly forms a second hand before dispersing.
scenarios.setup: A person reaches across a table toward an empty place beside a steaming mug.
scenarios.turn: The steam briefly echoes the shape of an offered hand.
scenarios.landing: They close their hand around their own cup and breathe out.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use a controlled composited silhouette rather than asking a model to form precise fingers in steam.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Strong visual metaphor, but the effect and interpretive ambiguity make it an advanced experiment.

scenarios.title: The Window Wave
scenarios.logline: A departing adult waves at a window; after the curtain closes, the older parent's hand stays against the glass.
scenarios.setup: From outside a house, a departing adult waves toward a familiar window.
scenarios.turn: Inside, the older parent closes the curtain but leaves one hand on the glass.
scenarios.landing: Outside, the departing adult turns back for one more wave.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Keep both sides of one window geographically locked; avoid showing a vehicle departure.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Recognizable longing with three shots and reflection risk.

scenarios.title: Same Old Handshake
scenarios.logline: An adult hesitates before an old robot, until it offers a distinctive two-knock greeting that the adult returns.
scenarios.setup: An adult pauses beside a dusty, powered-down-looking companion robot on a workshop bench.
scenarios.turn: Its eyes brighten; it raises a padded palm and makes two small familiar knocks on the bench.
scenarios.landing: Recognition softens the adult's face; they return two knocks and place a hand beside the robot's.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use side-by-side hands instead of interlocking fingers; repeat the visible two-knock pattern.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Distinctive repeated gesture supports recognition; audience testing must confirm it reads as reunion rather than first contact.

scenarios.title: The Familiar Scarf
scenarios.logline: A waiting adult spots a familiar scarf, then its wearer opens it to share exactly as they used to.
scenarios.setup: A waiting adult studies an approaching figure in a distinctive striped scarf.
scenarios.turn: The figure opens one end of the scarf toward the waiting adult.
scenarios.landing: They stand together under the same scarf and smile.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Keep the scarf's three-color pattern and end positions invariant.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Tender but requires a clear recognition performance rather than exposition.

scenarios.title: The Old Fetch
scenarios.logline: An adult offers a ball to an old dog, then sits beside it when the dog chooses company instead of fetch.
scenarios.setup: An adult kneels and offers a well-worn ball to a gray-muzzled dog.
scenarios.turn: The dog rests its head beside the ball rather than chasing it.
scenarios.landing: The adult puts the ball down and sits close, choosing stillness together.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Dog remains settled; no jump or running action. The story is companionship, not a proven long separation.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Strong adaptation of an expected ritual, with animal-contact reliability as the trade-off.

scenarios.title: The Repaired Kite
scenarios.logline: A repaired kite is offered across a gap between two adults; both take the same spool.
scenarios.setup: Two adults stand apart in a courtyard; one holds a visibly patched kite.
scenarios.turn: The kite and spool are offered across the empty space.
scenarios.landing: The second adult accepts the spool and closes the distance.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Keep kite grounded and strings minimal; do not claim viewers infer the whole friendship history.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Specific prop symbolism but a longer film may be needed for reconciliation to read.

scenarios.title: The Familiar Knock
scenarios.logline: A solitary adult sees a hand repeat an old tabletop rhythm, looks up and makes room for its owner.
scenarios.setup: An adult sits alone at a cafe table, idly tapping a distinctive rhythm.
scenarios.turn: Another hand enters and mirrors the same visible tap pattern.
scenarios.landing: The seated adult looks up, smiles and pulls the empty chair closer.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use two large slow taps, not a musical code that requires sound.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A human-scale recognition ritual with manageable motion.

scenarios.title: The Last Light
scenarios.logline: A small robot moves its final working lamp away from itself and toward a struggling seedling.
scenarios.setup: In a dim greenhouse, a small robot warms its own hands beneath a single lamp.
scenarios.turn: It notices a drooping seedling at the edge of the light and turns the lamp toward it.
scenarios.landing: The seedling is illuminated; the robot settles in shadow with a small steady eye light.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: No instant growth, extracted power core or death; edit between two motivated light states.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A visible resource trade-off with gentle fantasy, requiring deliberate lighting control.

scenarios.title: The Last Biscuit
scenarios.logline: Two friends each push the last biscuit toward the other, then break it and share.
scenarios.setup: One biscuit lies between two cups and two waiting adults.
scenarios.turn: Each person slides it toward the other; both notice the mirrored gesture.
scenarios.landing: The biscuit breaks into two pieces and both smile.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Cut from the intact biscuit to pre-broken halves rather than demanding a perfect generative fracture.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Very clear and inexpensive, but a well-established kindness trope.

scenarios.title: The Missed Train
scenarios.logline: A traveler lets a train leave while helping a stranger gather a spilled bag.
scenarios.setup: A traveler looks from an open train door to a bag spilled on the platform.
scenarios.turn: They kneel to help as the doors close behind them.
scenarios.landing: Both finish gathering the bag and share a relieved look.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Requires a major simplification to a stationary bus stop or offscreen departure before production.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Readable sacrifice but unsuitable for a low-cost first production as written.

scenarios.title: The Long Way Round
scenarios.logline: A tired adult discovers a cat asleep on their work chair and chooses a small stool instead.
scenarios.setup: A tired adult approaches a desk chair, ready to collapse into it.
scenarios.turn: A sleeping cat occupies the seat.
scenarios.landing: The adult pulls up a modest stool and works beside the undisturbed cat.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: The cat stays still; frame the chair and stool in the same readable space.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Simple and warm; familiar pet content means originality must come from character detail.

scenarios.title: The Only Flower
scenarios.logline: A person carrying one flower leaves it beside a stranger's worn memorial photograph instead of taking it home.
scenarios.setup: An adult carries one flower past another adult sitting with a framed photograph.
scenarios.turn: The flower is placed beside the photograph.
scenarios.landing: The recipient touches the stem and the giver steps away quietly.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Do not depend on reading the photo; test whether the intention is clear without a caption.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A restrained gesture, but memorial context could be inferred incorrectly.

scenarios.title: The Shadow Stays
scenarios.logline: A person walks away from a bench while a second shadow remains seated beside their own.
scenarios.setup: A person sits on a sunlit bench; two human shadows stretch across the ground.
scenarios.turn: The person stands, but one shadow remains seated.
scenarios.landing: They look back and gently wave to the remaining shadow.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Composite the second shadow as a separate layer; keep camera locked and do not request generative shadow physics.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Strong reframe, but compositing and interpretation make it a later pilot.

scenarios.title: The Door for a Dragon
scenarios.logline: An adult enlarges a tiny pet doorway to let a now-grown dragon rest its head inside.
scenarios.setup: A small pet doorway opens; a large gentle eye appears outside.
scenarios.turn: The adult opens the main door instead of shutting the little one.
scenarios.landing: A scaled head rests at the threshold and a hand settles beside it.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Reveal only the head; no full-body entrance or destructive door enlargement is needed.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Acceptance across changed scale, with a controllable partial creature reveal.

scenarios.title: The Paper Bird
scenarios.logline: A folded paper bird crosses a table and becomes real only after a waiting hand opens to receive it.
scenarios.setup: One adult slides an origami bird toward an empty open palm.
scenarios.turn: At the palm, paper wings become a small living bird.
scenarios.landing: The receiving hand opens wider and the bird rests rather than flying away.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use a graphic match between separate paper and living-bird keyframes, not a continuous anatomical transformation.
scenarios.scoreRationale: May read as a magic demonstration rather than connection; rewrite the emotional choice before production.

scenarios.title: The Mended Moon
scenarios.logline: One tiny moonkeeper uses a strip from their own glowing scarf to repair the other's dark lantern.
scenarios.setup: Two tiny figures sit on a rooftop; one lantern is dark.
scenarios.turn: The first figure wraps a glowing scarf end around the dark lantern handle.
scenarios.landing: Both lanterns glow softly as the figures lean together.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use stylized figures with simple silhouettes and cut between light states.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Specific shareable-resource metaphor without tragedy; more art-direction effort than a real-world prop story.

scenarios.title: The Last Hug
scenarios.logline: A partner's skin becomes bark during an offered embrace; the other person adjusts their arms around the changed shape.
scenarios.setup: Two adult partners move toward a familiar embrace in a quiet garden.
scenarios.turn: A matched pose reveals one partner as a gentle bark-covered figure.
scenarios.landing: The human partner pauses, then closes the embrace without withdrawing.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Preserve silhouette in two separate shots; no continuous body morph. Different setting, characters and imagery from the user's zombie reference.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Strong unconditional-acceptance mechanism but close to a familiar transformation trope and technically difficult.

scenarios.title: The Meeting Face
scenarios.relationship: adult and their own public/private persona
scenarios.logline: An impeccably composed video-call face is revealed to belong to someone wearing enormous cozy animal slippers.
scenarios.setup: An adult sits upright at a laptop in a formal jacket; framing suggests complete professional composure.
scenarios.turn: A clean wider view reveals absurdly oversized original-design slippers below the desk.
scenarios.landing: Without losing composure, they settle one slipper more comfortably and continue.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: No readable video-call interface needed; show slippers large enough for a phone and avoid copied character designs.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A familiar public/private contrast with a clear visual payoff; originality depends on fresh performance and design.

scenarios.title: The Important Visitor
scenarios.logline: An adult carefully prepares the best chair for an important guest; the guest is an unimpressed cat.
scenarios.setup: An adult straightens a cushion and presents a chair with excessive ceremony.
scenarios.turn: Cut to the same chair now occupied by an ordinary cat.
scenarios.landing: The adult takes a tiny stool beside it while the cat looks away.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use stable states rather than a cat jump; stylization is chosen before references, not applied as an inconsistent filter.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Clear benign status reversal, but a familiar pet joke rather than a novel premise.

scenarios.title: The Saving Expert
scenarios.logline: A person painstakingly squeezes the last trace from a tiny tube, surrounded by an extravagant pile of unopened plain parcels.
scenarios.setup: A meticulous adult rolls the end of a nearly empty unbranded tube.
scenarios.turn: A wider frame reveals a comically oversized stack of unopened plain delivery boxes.
scenarios.landing: They admire the tiny saved amount and carefully set the tube down.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Large readable tube action, stable boxes, no real brands or claims about a real person's finances.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Recognizable contradiction with original staging; cold viewers must connect the two visual facts.

scenarios.title: The Perfect Coaster
scenarios.logline: A person obsessively centers a mug on its coaster while the surrounding room is a mountain of harmless clutter.
scenarios.setup: Close view of a hand making a tiny final correction to a mug on a coaster.
scenarios.turn: The view widens to reveal an otherwise comically cluttered room.
scenarios.landing: One sock slips into view; the person nudges the coaster again, satisfied.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Keep clutter graphic and static; the sock can be in the second keyframe rather than simulated cloth motion.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Relatable behavior can work without a caption; visual hierarchy must stop clutter competing with the gag.

scenarios.title: The Marble Rematch
scenarios.logline: Two formally dressed adults rediscover a marble and quietly abandon dignity for a tiny floor game.
scenarios.setup: A marble rolls to a stop beside two pairs of grown-up shoes.
scenarios.turn: The adults exchange a competitive look and crouch on opposite sides.
scenarios.landing: One makes a simple flick; both break into a restrained grin.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Make marble large in initial composition; cut to a settled crouching state and simplify the flick.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Nostalgia is carried by a game and behavior rather than an assumed universal childhood.

scenarios.title: First-Rain Boats
scenarios.domain: universal ritual with subtle local texture
scenarios.logline: An adult sets a paper boat in a rain puddle; a neighbour's differently colored boat joins it.
scenarios.setup: An adult releases one small folded paper boat into a shallow safe puddle.
scenarios.turn: A second differently colored boat enters from the opposite side.
scenarios.landing: The two adults look up at each other and smile as the boats drift beside each other.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: No flooding or dangerous water; keep boats distinct and use one small puddle with modest motion.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Shared play is legible even for viewers without this exact childhood memory.

scenarios.title: Pocket of Daylight
scenarios.logline: A person folds a square of sunlight like paper and leaves it glowing in a dark corner.
scenarios.setup: A graphic square of warm light falls across an otherwise cool room.
scenarios.turn: In an explicitly stylized cut, the square becomes a folded luminous paper shape.
scenarios.landing: It rests in the dark corner, changing one small part of the room.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use original cut-paper style and two designed states; the nonphysical light behavior must be explicit, not disguised as photoreal accuracy.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A coherent visual metaphor rather than a character twist; audience interpretation remains untested.

scenarios.title: A Room of Seasons
scenarios.logline: The same hand rests around a cup while a window's leaf-shadow changes from spring to autumn.
scenarios.setup: A hand and cup sit in a graphic window-light composition.
scenarios.turn: Two deliberate matched states change the leaf-shadow pattern and outside season.
scenarios.landing: The hand draws the cup closer; the familiar room remains.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use stylized graphic state changes, not simulated months of continuous plant growth.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Atmosphere and continuity are the experience; no compulsory hidden tragedy or explanatory moral.

scenarios.title: The Under-Door Reply
scenarios.logline: One paper boat slips under a door; after a pause, a clearly different boat returns.
scenarios.setup: An adult hand sends a blue paper boat under a closed door.
scenarios.turn: A soft scrape accompanies a yellow boat emerging toward the waiting hand.
scenarios.landing: The hand places the yellow boat beside a spare blue one, accepting the reply.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Design a visibly adequate door gap and contrasting boat colors; no text message or inaccessible tiny clue.
scenarios.scoreRationale: A clear answer to an opening question; reciprocity must be evident rather than a boat merely bouncing back.

scenarios.title: The Knock in the Box
scenarios.logline: A mysterious box knocks from inside; opening it reveals a tiny robot politely knocking on the lid.
scenarios.setup: A plain closed box makes one visible small lid movement on a table.
scenarios.turn: An adult lifts the lid to reveal a tiny original robot with its paddle raised.
scenarios.landing: The adult knocks once on the tabletop; the robot answers.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: Use a cut from closed box to open stable state and one simple returned knock; no franchise design.
scenarios.scoreRationale: Mystery repaid by a benign comic social cue, with lid/hand contact as the main risk.

scenarios.title: A Seat for Dad
scenarios.logline: A boy removes the coat protecting a bench seat so his rain-soaked father can sit beside him.
scenarios.setup: The boy sits beside a coat-covered place while his father stands near the bench.
scenarios.turn: The boy lifts the coat onto his lap, revealing the dry seat he kept for his father.
scenarios.landing: Across a deliberate cut, father is already seated; they share a quiet familiar smile.
scenarios.feasibilityNote: One locked setup and a slightly tighter reaction; no animated sitting, hand intertwining, embrace or transformation. Generate and inspect all four endpoints before motion.
scenarios.scoreRationale: An editorial technical-pilot hypothesis, not a user rating: a visible small kindness and stable geography are easier to inspect than a spectacular transformation. Familiar mechanism; actual father-son reading and affect are untested.
